parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal law, no documented border/entry rules or police targeting, no documented violence pattern (data absent, not counted either way), and strongly documented social acceptance: two-decade pride growth, a 7th transgender march with international participants, described as among the region's most progressive. The surgical ID-marker requirement, conscription criteria and assisted-reproduction limits are resident-facing — the visitor uses a home passport and the dossier documents no official doubting foreign documents. Visitor-facing friction is modest: restroom discrimination (17% of reported incidents) and poorly implemented all-gender toilets, but no birth-sex exclusion rule; these are friction/hostility-lite, not state threat-framing. Rising anti-gender movement and the pride-hosting withdrawal are climate signals of backsliding pressure. Overall: acceptance with real but limited friction and no unremedied universal exposure — squarely the reduced-risk tier, ~0.75.
